status.label: Design ready — needs approval
status.detail: The crash path is narrowed to a cross-thread Shortcut Guide visibility check during Win-key release.

next_action.label: Approve the design and build the fix
next_action.reason: Approve the UI-thread visibility-state fix and implement it before more crash dumps or user repro rounds are collected.

design.root_cause: ShortcutGuide.App installs a low-level keyboard hook callback that reads OverlayWindow.AppWindow.IsVisible directly from the hook thread when Win is released. AppWindow is a WinUI/COM object owned by the UI thread; touching it from the native keyboard-hook thread while the overlay is hiding or switching panes can fault across the C++/WinRT boundary, which matches the fully reproducible crash when taskbar Win+number shortcuts are pressed while the taskbar pane is visible.
evidence: The issue is a fully reproducible crash in PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.exe whenever Win+number is pressed while taskbar labels are shown.
src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/App.xaml.cs reads OverlayWindow.AppWindow.IsVisible inside the low-level Win-key-up callback rather than on the UI thread.
The same file already marshals CloseAnimated back to OverlayWindow.DispatcherQueue, showing the code expects window operations to happen on the UI thread.
OverlayWindow.xaml.cs owns the show/hide lifecycle through ShowOverlay(), CloseAnimated(), and OnCloseTimerTick(), so a UI-thread visibility flag can replace cross-thread AppWindow property reads.

affected_files.purpose: Stop the hook thread from dereferencing AppWindow and use a UI-safe visibility signal instead.
Publish a UI-owned overlay-visible state that is updated in the show/hide lifecycle.
Add narrow regression coverage for the new visibility-state decision logic without needing a full WinUI window in tests.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Only AppWindow.Show()/Hide() reflects visibility, so non-UI code must read AppWindow.IsVisible to know whether the overlay is on screen.
implementation_steps.change: Add a lightweight UI-thread-owned visibility flag/property that is set true immediately before/after ShowOverlay and set false in the hide-timer completion path before AppWindow.Hide().
tests: Manual Win+number crash repro after the flag is introduced.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The Win-key-up hook callback and show-event listener branch on OverlayWindow.AppWindow.IsVisible from non-UI threads.
implementation_steps.change: Replace every non-UI AppWindow.IsVisible check with the new OverlayWindow.IsOverlayVisibleForHooks flag, and keep all real UI work inside DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue().
tests: Add a unit test or extracted helper test that verifies the close/no-close decision is based only on the flag.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: There is no regression coverage for the show/hide state used by the keyboard hook, so cross-thread visibility regressions are easy to reintroduce.
implementation_steps.change: Add a focused unit-test surface for the extracted visibility/close-decision helper so the hook path can be validated without instantiating a real WinUI AppWindow.
tests: Add unit coverage for visible vs hidden hook decisions.
Keep existing Shortcut Guide converter/unit tests green.

verify: Build Shortcut Guide.Ui and ShortcutGuide.UnitTests in x64 Debug or Release using the repo build scripts.
Run the new ShortcutGuide.UnitTests visibility-state tests.

Manually reproduce: open Shortcut Guide, wait for Win+number taskbar labels, press Win+1/Win+2/Win+3 repeatedly, and confirm the target app activates without crashing ShortcutGuide.exe or producing a dump.
Verify ordinary long-press Win, Esc close, and click-outside close behavior still work after the visibility flag change.
risks: If any show/hide path forgets to update the new flag, the overlay may stop closing on Win release or may close when it should remain visible.
The close animation timer means visibility transitions are intentionally asynchronous; the flag must represent “hook-visible” semantics, not just AppWindow current state.
Hook-thread logic must continue to avoid feedback loops when injected key-up events are replayed.
alternatives: Catching the crash around AppWindow.IsVisible is not viable because access violations and apartment violations can terminate the process before managed catch logic helps.
Marshalling every visibility query back to the UI thread adds latency on the hook path and still races the taskbar Win+number gesture.
Disabling Win+number handling while Shortcut Guide is open would avoid the crash but would regress a legitimate Windows shortcut.
